Porch visual principles

Every visual decision should help tired eyes rest on Scripture—not compete with it. This page is the quiet reference for the May 2026 polish pass.

Measure: Can someone take a slow breath here?

Eight principles

  1. Scripture first. KJV text is the hero. One primary focal block per screen.
  2. Breathing room. Generous vertical rhythm; readable line length on phones.
  3. Soft edges, quiet depth. Porch cards, subtle shadow, no engagement motion on spiritual content.
  4. Typography like a well-loved page. Comfortable line-height; 44px+ tap targets on verse controls.
  5. Contrast without harshness. Soft blues and greys; gold accents sparingly; visible focus rings.
  6. Nothing demands attention. No streaks, scores, or guilt widgets.
  7. Kids Corner exception (bounded). Playful sky in Kids paths only; KJV ref stays tiny and honest.
  8. Measure rest, not dazzle. Not “does this look trending?” but “does the Word land with less strain?”

Where it lives in code

  • tdb-visual-tokens.css — shared spacing, porch surfaces, polish overrides
  • tdb-home-page.css — home layout only
  • styles.css — inner pages
  • Verse image porch presets — calm background directions
  • Home daily verse — optional device-only restfulness note

What changed this season

  • Calmer verse body line-height and breath divider on Home
  • Battle Plans hero subtitle width for one-glance reading
  • Kids welcome band on sky backgrounds
  • Five porch-calm image prompts + two new free verse-image starters
